site.locationBasis: User-provided Sternicza 11 map pin; plot orientation comes from the mapped EPSG:2180 local basis.
site.orientationNote: Spherical transverse-Mercator convergence atan(tan(longitude − 19°) × sin(latitude)); grid azimuth = true azimuth − convergence. The correction is approximately −0.300° here. An independent pyproj check returned −0.29988185370627357°, agreeing within 0.000001°.

sources.title: NOAA — solar calculation details
sources.details: Meeus-based solar position, uncertainty of sunrise/set and distinction between atmospheric refraction and geometric angles. This app uses its own implementation and does not depend on NOAA's retired calculator service.

sources.title: NOAA — general solar position equations
sources.details: Clockwise-from-north azimuth, true solar time and the conventional −0.833° sunrise/sunset horizon. The implementation uses Julian-century orbital equations rather than the shorter fractional-year approximation in this overview.

sources.title: NREL — Solar Position Algorithm reference example
sources.details: Reda and Andreas, NREL/TP-560-34302. The 2003-10-17 example independently checks the implemented azimuth and geometric elevation. The simulator does not claim the much tighter accuracy of the full SPA algorithm.

sources.title: pvlib — independent NREL SPA implementation used for validation
sources.details: Independent reference values at 08:00, 12:00, 16:00 and 20:00 on four seasonal dates in 2026 agreed within 0.02° for both azimuth and geometric elevation. Validation only: pvlib is not shipped as an application dependency.

sources.title: PROJ — transverse Mercator projection
sources.details: Projected-grid orientation differs from geographic north; the mapped local basis is corrected for site meridian convergence before positioning the sun.

sources.title: GeographicLib — meridian convergence convention
sources.details: Convergence is the clockwise bearing of grid north from true north; used to verify the sign of the rotation.

sources.title: ECMA-402 — IANA time-zone database use
sources.details: Local dates and times resolve with Intl.DateTimeFormat using Europe/Warsaw, independent of the computer's own timezone. Future timezone-rule changes depend on the browser's timezone database.

assumptions: Date input supports 2000–2100. The default view is 21 June 2026 at 12:00 Europe/Warsaw; this is an illustrative summer scenario, not the current time.
Azimuth is measured clockwise from true north; elevation is degrees above a level geometric horizon. Direct-light rays use the geometric centre of the sun.
Sunrise and sunset are apparent-horizon estimates using −0.833° for the solar disc and standard atmospheric refraction. Buildings and trees can delay direct sun at the property.
The first occurrence is used for the repeated autumn DST hour. A nonexistent spring hour shifts forward by the gap; the interface receives an explicit explanatory note.
No cloud cover, diffuse-sky light, irradiance, glare or thermal load is predicted. Low-elevation atmospheric effects and uncertain building/vegetation geometry limit shadow precision.
